title: debug - 5be1911c
description:
Looking at the error, the root cause is clear: the `StylometricCNN` module uses `input_ids` (which are BPE token IDs from DistilBERT, ranging from 0 to ~30K) but its `nn.Embedding` layer has `vocab_size=128`. This causes index out-of-bounds errors. The fix is to properly pass character-level token IDs to the CNN, not the BPE token IDs.

Let me implement the fix:
method: The code implements a multi-view text classification model for author attribution. It extracts 59 stylometric features (character counts, punctuation, lexical diversity, readability scores, etc.) from text. The model architecture fuses three views: DistilBERT embeddings (768-dim), a character-level CNN with multi-scale convolutions (kernels 2-5), and an MLP on stylometric features. These are concatenated and passed through a classifier with LayerNorm and dropout. Training uses stratified 80/20 split, class-weighted cross-entropy loss, AdamW optimizer with separate learning rates (2e-5 for BERT, 2e-4 for custom layers), cosine annealing scheduler with warm restarts, gradient clipping, and mixed precision. Early stopping with patience 5 is used, and the best model is selected by validation loss.

title: debug - e0238546
description:
Looking at the error, the root cause is clear: NaN values in model predictions during validation. This is a common issue when using DeBERTa-v3-large with high learning rates — the model can produce unstable outputs, especially with the complex cross-attention architecture. 

The fix strategy needs to:
1. Reduce learning rates significantly to prevent gradient explosion
2. Add gradient clipping and stabilize the AdamW optimizer
3. Use lower learning rates for the transformer backbone (5e-6 instead of 2e-5)
4. Add input validation to catch NaN predictions early

Here are the targeted code fixes:
method: Data preprocessing included cleaning text (whitespace normalization) and label encoding authors. Feature engineering extracted character n-grams (2-5, 1000 features), word n-grams (1-3, 2000 features) via TF-IDF, and 15 punctuation/style features (punctuation counts, capitalization ratio, avg word length). The model architecture combined a DeBERTa-v3-large transformer with a stylometric encoder (MLP with LayerNorm and GELU), cross-attention between CLS token and stylometric features, and a fused classifier head. Training used stratified 80/20 split, 8-epoch training with early stopping (patience=5), AdamW optimizer with differential learning rates (5e-6 for transformer, 5e-4 for others), label smoothing (0.1), gradient accumulation (2 steps), mixed precision (AMP), and gradient clipping. Validation metric was log loss (lower is better).

title: debug - ccb090d0
description:
Looking at the error, the model is producing NaN predictions. This is happening because of the progressive unfreezing strategy combined with aggressive mixed precision training. The model's backbone (DeBERTa) was frozen for the first epochs, and the classifier head alone cannot learn meaningful representations from the frozen backbone. Additionally, the `autocast` context manager with the frozen backbone can cause numerical instability leading to NaN gradients.

The fix is to:
1. Keep the DeBERTa backbone unfrozen from the start (since we're fine-tuning a pretrained model, all layers should be trainable)
2. Use a simpler training approach without progressive unfreezing
3. Use a smaller, more efficient model like `microsoft/deberta-v3-small` to speed up training and reduce memory issues
4. Set `TOKENIZERS_PARALLELISM=false` to suppress the fork warnings
5. Add gradient clipping and NaN detection
method: The code loads text data from CSV, applies basic cleaning, and engineers 27 stylometric features (character/word/sentence counts, punctuation ratios, POS-tag ratios, etc.). It also extracts character n-grams (2–5) and word TF-IDF (1–3) features. A DeBERTa-v3-small transformer is fine-tuned with 5-fold stratified cross-validation, using AdamW optimizer with different learning rates for backbone (2e-5) and classifier (5e-5), cosine schedule with warmup, gradient clipping, and early stopping. Final test predictions are averaged across folds and formatted into a submission CSV.

title: debug - 85c3e389
description:
Looking at the error, the core problem is clear: severe overfitting with training loss dropping to 0.08 while validation loss rises to 0.85, far above the best of 0.467 at epoch 3. The model is too large (435M parameters for DeBERTa-v3-large) and overfits rapidly on this small dataset. Additionally, the submission was saved with a random suffix name instead of the exact required path `./submission/submission.csv`.

The fix strategy:
1. Switch to a smaller, more efficient model (`microsoft/deberta-v3-small` with ~183M params) to reduce overfitting and speed training
2. Add stronger regularization: higher dropout, weight decay, and gradient clipping
3. Use a lower learning rate (5e-6) for the backbone to prevent catastrophic forgetting
4. Fix the submission path to exactly `./submission/submission.csv`
5. Set `TOKENIZERS_PARALLELISM=false` to suppress fork warnings
6. Use Real-Time Validation at best epoch (not just at end) with proper metric reporting
7. Use a proper consistency check: same processing for val and test
method: The code loads a Kaggle dataset for author identification (EAP, HPL, MWS) and uses a stratified 5-fold split to create a single train/validation partition. It tokenizes text using microsoft/deberta-v3-small with a max length of 384. The model wraps a DebertaV2ForSequenceClassification in a TemperatureScaledModel for logit scaling, trained with AdamW (weight decay 0.1, lr 5e-6), linear warmup scheduler, mixed precision (AMP), gradient clipping, and early stopping (patience 3) over up to 12 epochs. Validation uses log loss (multi-class cross-entropy). The best model is used for test inference and submission generation.
